provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Each 4-connected object of the single foreground colour (palette[3]) on background palette[0] is recoloured in place by its shape topology: if any cell has >=3 orthogonal same-object neighbours (a branch/T-junction, from the 'aitch' sprite) it becomes palette[2]; otherwise if it has >=2 corner cells (exactly one horizontal and one vertical neighbour, i.e. a U/C path) it becomes palette[6]; otherwise (a single-bend L) it becomes palette[1]. Neighbour counts, branch cells and corner cells are invariant under all D4 transforms (a rotation merely swaps horizontal and vertical counts, which the corner test treats symmetrically), so the emitted program works directly on visible coordinates with no axis specialization; only colour constants are specialized via the palette.
draft_notes.limitations: Relies on the constructor's non-overlap check (margin 1) keeping sprites from touching orthogonally; if two sprites touched they would merge into one component. Classification assumes rand_sprite 'el' always yields exactly one bend, 'you' at least two bends without branches, and 'aitch' always contains a junction cell, as the archived solver and fixtures indicate; the common.rand_sprite source was not shown, so any degenerate sprite variant (e.g. a straight bar) would fall to colour palette[1]. No tests were run.
draft_notes.host_review: Keep independently sampled topology types; do not force every pair to contain all categories. Episode gate requires output-colour evidence per query topology (branch H, two-or-more corners U, remaining L). Replace simultaneous overlap lottery with bounded randomized rectangle backtracking; maintain original h10..20,w=h+-2,N=1+max(h,w)//3, sizes3..5, spacing1 and native random_sprite. Placement probabilities change, no lattice/tiny-shape fallback. Explicit fixture calls unchanged.
draft_notes.semantic_draft_review: Opus5.5 subscription CLI draft reviewed; evidence handled at episode level, not by removing native simple scenes.
